intent.task: know what did and did NOT happen in each workstream independently, without inferring a shared cause or hierarchy that isn't there
intent.rationale: negations here are load-bearing -- dropping a negation changes what the fact means, not just how much detail survives

questions.question: What does the security audit explicitly not cover?
Is the gap in third-party dependency coverage an oversight or a deliberate scope decision?
questions.gold_answer: Deliberate — it's tracked as a separate future effort, not an oversight.

questions.question: Was the database found to be the bottleneck in the performance investigation?
questions.gold_answer: No — it was explicitly ruled out; query times were normal.

questions.question: If not the database, what was the actual bottleneck?
questions.gold_answer: An unoptimized client-side rendering path re-running the same computation on every scroll event.

questions.question: Is the hiring push increasing the team's headcount?
questions.gold_answer: No — it's backfilling exactly one departure, not expanding headcount.

questions.question: Does the hiring push depend on or relate to any of the other three workstreams?
questions.gold_answer: No — it has no connection to them and isn't motivated by their findings.

questions.question: Does the docs overhaul depend on the security audit finishing first?
questions.gold_answer: No — they have no dependency on each other; they just happen to run in the same quarter.

questions.question: Are the four workstreams organized under a shared parent category, or are they independent peers?
questions.gold_answer: Independent peers — none is a sub-part of another and they share no parent theme beyond the quarter.
